personas.description: Investigative analyst researching recipients of Mexican public contracts and their legitimacy.
Oversight stakeholder verifying supplier integrity against registries and sanctions lists.

jobs_to_be_done.description: Identify who receives public money in Mexico through government contracts.
Assess whether contract recipients are legitimate companies using public evidence.
Cross-check supplier profiles against registries and sanctions lists.

requirements.description: Link at least 50 suppliers to real public contracts, each with evidence-backed contract references.
Build a core profile per supplier: identity, address, founding date, tax-list status, sanction status.
Ensure at least 80% of linked suppliers have a complete core profile.
Use US sanctions and registry lists only as secondary cross-checks, never as primary authority.
Record zero profile values without evidence; every field must cite a source.
Draw evidence from at least 4 distinct source classes (e.g., contracts, registries, sanctions, news).

constraints: Public read-only sources only; no paywalled or private data.
Run budget: USD 2.0; scope must fit this budget.
Elapsed run time unknown until execution; targets must not assume fixed runtime.
Every profile value must carry evidence; no unsourced values.
US sanctions/registry lists used only as secondary cross-checks.
Proposed domains are hypotheses for human review, never captured evidence.
non_goals: No private, leaked, or paywalled data sources.
No primary reliance on US sanctions/registry lists for legitimacy judgments.
No exhaustive coverage of all Mexican contract recipients.
No legal determinations of fraud or wrongdoing; evidence assembly only.
No runtime or performance guarantees before execution.

trusted_publishers.rationale: Official Mexican public contract records; authoritative source for contract links.

trusted_publishers.kind: Mexican business registries and tax authority (e.g., SAT, REPSE)
trusted_publishers.rationale: Official registries authoritative for identity, address, founding date, tax-list status.

trusted_publishers.kind: US sanctions and registry lists (e.g., OFAC)
trusted_publishers.rationale: Human revision: secondary cross-checks only, never primary authority.

trusted_publishers.kind: Reputable news and civil-society oversight outlets
trusted_publishers.rationale: Supplementary context; uncertain authority, requires human review.
Supplementary cross-checks requested by human revision; never auto authority.

DoD must be the case's: >=50 suppliers linked to real public contracts; >=80% of them with a complete core profile (identity, address, founding date, tax-list status, sanction status); 0 values without evidence; >=4 source classes. Keep US sanctions/registry lists as secondary cross-checks.

definition_of_done.metric: Suppliers linked to real public contracts with evidence-backed contract references
definition_of_done.basis_quote: >=50 suppliers linked to real public contracts
definition_of_done.rationale: Human revision sets explicit threshold of 50 linked suppliers.
definition_of_done.feasibility: Achievable within USD 2.0 using public Mexican contracting data; runtime unknown but query count is bounded.

definition_of_done.metric: Linked suppliers with complete core profile (identity, address, founding date, tax-list status, sanction status)
definition_of_done.basis_quote: >=80% of them with a complete core profile (identity, address, founding date, tax-list status, sanction status)
definition_of_done.rationale: Human revision requires 80% completeness ratio across linked suppliers.
definition_of_done.feasibility: Feasible with public registries; some suppliers may lack public data, 80% allows margin.

definition_of_done.rationale: Human revision requires zero unsourced values.
definition_of_done.feasibility: Enforceable by validation; no budget impact.

definition_of_done.metric: Distinct source classes used for evidence
definition_of_done.rationale: Human revision requires at least four distinct source classes.
definition_of_done.feasibility: Contracts, registries, sanctions, and news are all public and free; fits USD 2.0.
